2026-09-30.meal: Sunday's ratatouille, reheated, with bread or rice

steps: Tip the ratatouille into a pan with a splash of water.
Heat gently, stirring, until it bubbles and is piping hot all the way through (about 8 minutes).
Or microwave in a covered bowl for 4–5 minutes, stirring halfway.
Serve with bread or rice, and a sprinkle of cheese if you like.
recipe.tip: Only reheat it once. Anyone eating after hockey can have their portion microwaved separately.

ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil + knob of butter
50g parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, grated
steps: Soften the leeks in the oil and butter for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and garlic and cook for 5 more.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute until coated.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, letting each one soak in before the next. It takes about 20 minutes.
When the rice is tender but still has a little bite, take it off the heat.
Stir in the cheese and crème fraîche, season, cover and rest for 2 minutes before serving.
recipe.tip: Oven shortcut: after step 2, add all the stock, cover and bake at 180°C for 25 minutes, then stir in the cheese.

2026-10-02.note: Normal evening — gymnastics 9:30am & swimming 1:30pm today, nothing on for tea

ingredients: 2 nests medium egg noodles (or 300g straight-to-wok noodles)
steps: If using dried noodles, cook per pack instructions, then drain and set aside.
Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan over a high heat. Stir-fry the pepper, carrot and sugar snaps for 3-4 minutes until just softening.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Push the veg to one side, add the prawns and cook for 2-3 minutes until pink and cooked through.
Take out Mathilda's portion of veg, noodles and prawns now, and toss with just a little plain soy.
Add the noodles, soy sauce and chilli sauce to the rest and toss for 1-2 minutes until piping hot.
Scatter with spring onions and serve with lime wedges.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep her portion plain — a little soy only, no chilli sauce. Swap prawns for chicken if that's what's in.

2026-10-03.note: This week's one meat night. Hockey open session 9:15am then the away match at Sheffield (1:40-2:40pm) — slow cooker on before we leave so tea's ready when we're back

ingredients: 1 tbsp cornflour, mixed with a splash of water
Crusty bread or mash, to serve
steps: Put the onion, carrots, celery and leeks into the slow cooker.
Add the chicken thighs on top, then the tomatoes, stock, tomato purée and thyme. Season.
Cover and cook on low for 6-7 hours (or high for 3-4) until the chicken is tender and falling apart.
About 20 minutes before serving, stir in the cornflour slurry to thicken, and shred the chicken through the sauce.
Serve with crusty bread or mash.
recipe.tip: On by 8am before we leave for hockey/the match. Mathilda: mash her portion with a fork and check for bones. Freeze any leftovers fully cooled, portioned and labelled for the meal drawer.

2026-10-04.note: Free day — double batch: eat tonight, freeze 4 portions for Tuesday after Hull hockey training

ingredients: 1 veg stock cube, dissolved in 300ml water
Parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, to serve
steps: Soften the onions, garlic, carrots and celery in the oil for 8-10 minutes.
Stir in the lentils, passata, tomato purée, herbs and stock. Season.
Cover and simmer gently for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and the lentils are tender.
Cook the spaghetti per pack instructions and drain.
Take out Mathilda's portion, and the 4 portions to freeze, before adding any extra pepper or chilli flakes to the rest.
Serve the sauce over spaghetti with grated cheese.
Cool the 4 freezer portions within an hour, then pack into labelled tubs and freeze flat for Tuesday.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: mash the lentils a little finer if she's fussy about texture. A meal-drawer regular — freezes really well.

2026-10-05.meal: Fish finger pitta pockets with slaw
2026-10-05.note: Quiet Monday, nothing on for tea

ingredients: 1/4 white or red cabbage, finely shredded
Ketchup or tartare sauce, to serve
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and cook the fish fingers for 12-15 minutes, turning once, until golden and piping hot (or air-fryer: 180°C for 10 minutes, turning halfway).
Mix the cabbage and carrot with the mayonnaise and lemon juice to make the slaw. Season.
Warm the pittas briefly and split open.
Fill each pitta with lettuce, 3 fish fingers and a spoonful of slaw.
Serve with ketchup or tartare sauce on the side.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: fish fingers and pitta plain, slaw on the side so she can dip or avoid it. Cut her pitta into fingers.

2026-10-06.note: Hull hockey training 6-7pm (Hymers College) plus travel — tea ready for whoever's not driving, kept warm for the rest

ingredients: 4 frozen portions of Sunday's lentil bolognese
Parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, to serve
steps: Defrost the bolognese portions overnight in the fridge, or use the microwave defrost setting.

Tip into a pan with a splash of water and heat gently, stirring, until bubbling and piping hot all the way through (about 8-10 minutes). Or microwave in a covered bowl for 5-6 minutes, stirring halfway.
Cook fresh spaghetti while the sauce heats.
Serve with grated cheese. Anyone back late from hockey can have their portion microwaved separately.
recipe.tip: Only reheat each portion once, and check it's piping hot all the way through before serving.

2026-10-07.meal: Air-fryer veggie sausages with crispy potato wedges & beans
2026-10-07.note: Hockey Academy Night 6:15-7:45pm (The Lindum) — air fryer gets tea done fast either side of the run

ingredients: 1/2 tsp smoked paprika (for the grown-ups' wedges)
steps: Toss the potato wedges in the oil, season, and air fry at 200°C for 12 minutes.
Add the paprika to the wedges for the grown-ups now, keeping Mathilda and Francis's plain.
Add the veggie sausages to the air fryer basket alongside the wedges and cook for a further 8-10 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and the wedges are crisp.
Heat the beans in a small pan or the microwave for 3-4 minutes.
Serve the sausages and wedges with the beans.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: cut her sausage into coins and keep her wedges plain. Ready in 20 minutes either side of hockey academy.

2026-10-08.meal: Air-fryer breaded fish fillets with mash, peas & sweetcorn
2026-10-08.note: Early tea before Francis's parents' evening appointment at 7:05pm — ready in about 20 minutes

ingredients: 2 microwave mash pouches (or 500g potatoes, peeled and chunked)
steps: Preheat the air fryer to 200°C. Air fry the fish fillets for 10-12 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and piping hot.
Meanwhile heat the mash pouches in the microwave per pack instructions (or boil the potato chunks for 12-15 minutes, then drain and mash with the butter and milk).
Cook the peas and sweetcorn in a pan of boiling water for 3-4 minutes, then drain.
Serve the fish fillets with the mash, peas and sweetcorn.
recipe.tip: Use the microwave mash pouches for real speed before parents' evening — ready in under 20 minutes total. Mathilda: flake her fish and check for bones.
